transcript:
Header: 2026-11-04 15:30 UTC | Duration 58 minutes | Recording ID ff-20261104-fuseworks-01
Attendees: Sanjay Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Morales (Redwood SE), Iris Chen (Redwood CSM), Maya Thompson (FuseWorks Head of Platforms), Jon Rivera (Cloud Architect), Priya Kapoor (Partnerships), Leo Zhang (Security)

Summary: Sprint planning for joint marketplace listing and reference architecture. Focus areas: listing assets, deployment IaC, integration test plan, cost/metering hooks, security signoffs. Agreed to pilot window mid-November; Redwood to deliver listing draft and IaC examples.

Topics: marketplace packaging, reference architecture docs, CI/CD for private deployments, billing and metering events, security/compliance checklist, pilot success criteria

Action items: See metadata fields.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sanjay: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I see Maya, Jon, Priya, Leo — great. We'll keep this to about an hour, agenda's in the doc I shared.
[00:18] Maya: Yep thanks, Sanjay. We're excited, trying to get the listing live before Black Friday for our customers in NA.
[00:26] Jon: Timing's tight, we need to validate private deployment patterns in our VPC and the cost profile — especially during peak traffic.
[00:35] Lena: Totally. Today we wanted to align on what Redwood needs for the marketplace tile and the joint-ref arch, plus what FuseWorks needs from our side for the pilot.
[00:44] Priya: And also the co-marketing assets — logos, screenshots, short demo video. We have a studio but need the product screenshots styled.
[00:52] Sanjay: Perfect. Quick clarification — by marketplace listing do you mean the cloud marketplace tile and the 'bring your own infra' reference arch on our docs site? Or also a packaged SaaS listing?
[01:05] Maya: Both, ideally. We want a marketplace tile for quick onboarding, but the reference arch needs to show Dedicated and Private deployment flows with our networking patterns.
[01:15] Lena: Okay makes sense. For the tile we'll need: short description, one-pager, a couple of screenshots, and a deploy link that points to an L1 onboarding runbook. For the refarch we'll produce Terraform + Helm snippets and a sample pipeline.
[01:26] Jon: On the infra side, our main constraints are: transit gateway peering to Redwood's private control plane, strict egress rules, and we must keep logs in our KMS key for at-rest encryption.
[01:40] Leo: From security, SOC 2 Type II is a must, SSO SAML flow that supports SCIM for provisioning, and we need audit logs sent to our SIEM. Also asking about key management — are you able to integrate with customer-managed K M S or H S M?
[01:56] Sanjay: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer K M S integration, and we can provide a KMS binder doc. We'll share our SOC2 pack; Iris will attach it. Regarding SCIM/SAML we have a SSO guide.
[02:10] Iris: I'll follow up with the SOC2 link and our KMS integration doc after the call.
[02:16] Priya: On licensing and billing — how does metering look for a Dedicated deployment? We need per-token-style billing or an instance-hour model for our procurement.
[02:27] Lena: We can expose metering hooks. Typically we show both: token-equivalent metrics in the UI and a flat instance-hour for reserved capacity. For the marketplace tile we need to decide which one to surface.
[02:38] Jon: The procurement team leans to instance-hour for simplicity, but engineering needs the token breakdown to correlate cost to workload.
[02:46] Sanjay: Common trade-off. For the pilot let's do instance-hour for billing and we will export token logs for engineering to analyze. That satisfies procurement and gives you the cost observability you need.
[02:58] Maya: That works. For pilot success criteria: <1s p50 latency on 8k prompt, stable throughput of 30 rps, and automated deployment reproducible through Terraform.
[03:11] Lena: Good clear goals — we'll include an evaluation harness. Also we recommend enabling KV cache for your prefix-heavy workflows to reduce token cost.
[03:21] Jon: Quick question — what's the recommended quantization profile for our A100-ish fleet if we want better latency/cost? Any prebuilt model variants from Redwood?
[03:32] Lena: We have a recommended matrix — we'll send it. Short answer: int8 with 4-bit KV where possible; some models we host have 'fast' variants with trimmed kv cache footprint. I'll post the model-performance sheet.
[03:44] Priya: Will that require any code changes on our side or is it purely server-side on Redwood?
[03:50] Lena: Mostly server-side. There's a small flag in the inference SDK if you want to pin variants for compatibility.
[03:55] Jon: Okay good. Now on the CI/CD side — we need an example pipeline for running integration tests that spin up a ephemeral dedicated instance, run smoke tests and tear down. Do you have a template?
[04:08] Sanjay: Yes, Lena has the pipeline template. Lena, can you walk through the proposed steps?
[04:13] Lena: Sure — the pipeline will: 1) bootstrap infra via Terraform apply (control plane endpoint + networking), 2) deploy the Redwood runtime via Helm chart, 3) run smoke tests hitting the inference API with a test prompt set, 4) gather logs and token metrics, 5) destroy the environment. We'll share a GitHub Actions and Jenkins example.
[04:35] Jon: Great. On step 3, the smoke tests — can we include latency budgets and token distribution checks?
[04:42] Lena: Yes, the harness will include p50/p95/p99 and a token distribution histogram. Note that the initial harness won't be perfect — we'll tune it during the pilot.
[04:52] Leo: For audit logs — can your runtime redact PII before logs ship to our SIEM? We need to avoid storing customer-provided PII in third-party logs.
[05:02] Sanjay: We have configurable log masking rules; we can either redact at the runtime or send raw logs to your VPC where your logging pipeline handles redaction. We'll document both patterns.
[05:13] Maya: Sounds good. On the listing assets timeline — what's the earliest you can deliver the marketplace draft? We need to review legal and marketing.
[05:22] Sanjay: We can share a draft listing and the one-pager by Friday, Nov 6. That will include a proposed pricing blurb, screenshots, and a short 90-second demo script.
[05:34] Priya: If we get those by Friday we can turn around the assets in a week. Also request: can you provide a short recording of a live deploy flow we can clip into our listing?
[05:45] Lena: Yes, I can record a screencast showing terraform apply and a sample inference call — I'll keep it under 2 minutes.
[05:53] Jon: Anything about network: we have strict egress rules — will Redwood require a static outbound IP so we can allowlist?
[06:02] Lena: For Private deploys you own the outbound; for Dedicated we can provision static egress IPs per tenancy. We'll detail that in the network appendix.
[06:13] Maya: Great. I'm a little worried about the scale test — our internal QA saw a spike causing the instance scheduler to throttle during ramp. How do you handle graceful degradation?
[06:25] Sanjay: Redwood has routing tiers and automatic fallback to multi-variant models for graceful degradation. For Dedicated we can provision burst capacity and autoscaling guards to avoid scheduler tight loops.
[06:36] Jon: Can we put a quota guard in the pipeline to prevent runaway token consumption during the smoke tests?
[06:41] Lena: Yes, the harness supports token caps and simulated throttling to validate your business logic.
[06:49] Priya: Any competitor features we should be aware of that customers often ask about?
[06:54] Sanjay: Customers compare us to Anthropic and cloud vendor endpoints — differences are around cost controls and private deployment options. Also some teams layer Pinecone for vector store integration; we recommend a vetted connector.
[07:07] Leo: On compliance, will you sign a DPA and support data residency in EU? We have EU customers who need their inference logs stored in EU regions.
[07:16] Iris: We support region pinning for hosted and private modes; DPA is standard, we'll route the legal request post-call.
[07:24] Maya: Ok recap and next steps? I'd like a checklist we can use with our engineers to prepare for the pilot.
[07:30] Sanjay: Recap: Redwood to send marketplace draft + SOC2 + K M S doc by Nov 6. Lena to publish Terraform and pipeline samples by Nov 9. FuseWorks to confirm pilot participants and test data by Nov 10. Pilot window planned Nov 16-20.
[07:46] Priya: We'll also prepare the co-marketing assets and confirm a short press memo timeline; likely no press until after pilot.
[07:55] Sanjay: Great. Any blockers?
[07:58] Jon: Need the Terraform module sample to unblock our infra spike tests.
[08:02] Lena: I'll mark it high priority.
[08:05] Maya: Thanks everyone. Iris, please add the SOC2 link and the redwood contact list.
[08:10] Iris: Will do.
[08:12] Sanjay: Ok we'll follow up in Asana and attach the doc links. Thanks all.

[58:00] Meeting ends.

References mentioned: 'marketplace draft doc', 'Terraform module repo (to be shared)', 'SOC2 pack (Iris)', 'KMS integration guide', 'model-performance matrix (Lena)'

Transcript notes: occasional ASR errors may exist (e.g., "K M S" spaced out, 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K V cash'), speaker labeling approximated where participants talked over each other.
